topIssues.title: proxyd: consensus mode answers out-of-range state reads and log ranges with placeholder results
topIssues.author: tremarkley
topIssues.body:
## Summary

Since #552, a `consensus_aware` backend group answers a request for a block above proxyd's consensus latest without forwarding it (`OverwriteConsensusResponses` in `proxyd/backend.go`). For block lookups the answer is `null`, which is correct. For state reads it returns a placeholder value:

| Method | proxyd answers | The op-reth backend answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eth_getBalance`, `eth_getTransactionCount` | `"0x0"` | `-32001 block not found` |
| `eth_getCode` | `"0x"` | `-32001 block not found` |
| `eth_getStorageAt` | 32 zero bytes | `-32001 block not found` |
| `eth_call`, `eth_getProof` | `null` | `-32001 block not found` |
| `eth_getLogs`, range past the head | `[]` | `-32602 block range extends beyond current head block` |

A client can't tell these from real values: a zero balance or nonce, a contract with no code, an empty storage slot, a range with no events.

`eth_getLogs` is the worst case. A range that only partly crosses the consensus head also gets `[]`, dropping the logs of the blocks that do exist. Checked on a consensus-aware mainnet deployment with `fromBlock` = head − 5 and `toBlock` = head + 50: proxyd answered `[]`, while the op-reth backend answered `-32602`. A poller that then advances its cursor loses those events for good. Execution clients return an error for state at an unknown block (geth `header not found`, reth `-32001 block not found`).

## Impact

proxyd runs several replicas, and each polls its own consensus latest. A client that sees block N on one replica and then reads state at N can land on a replica still at N−1, and gets a placeholder zero.

We hit this with a Ponder indexer reading `eth_getBalance` at each new head. It stored zero balances for about 3% of sampled blocks. Its `eth_call` reads were unaffected only because Ponder retries a `null` `eth_call` result.

## Reproduce

Against any consensus-aware deployment whose consensus latest is `L`:

```bash
curl -s "$PROXYD_URL" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_getBalance","params":["0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000011","<L + 50, hex>"]}'
# {"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":"0x0","id":1}
```

The same request sent to any backend directly returns `{"error":{"code":-32001,"message":"block not found: 0x…"}}`.

## Proposed fix

- Keep `null` for block lookups, which is also what op-reth returns.
- Return the error an execution client would, with HTTP 200, which keeps #552's goal of not answering HTTP 400:
  - for `eth_getBalance`, `eth_getTransactionCount`, `eth_getCode`, `eth_getStorageAt`, `eth_getProof` and `eth_call`: `{"code": -32001, "message": "block not found"}`. `-32001` is EIP-1474's "Resource not found" and matches op-reth;
  - for `eth_getLogs` and `eth_newFilter`: `{"code": -32602, "message": "block range extends beyond current head block"}`. That is what both op-geth and op-reth return for `eth_getLogs`; `eth_newFilter` previously got a `null` filter id.
- Clients that retry on errors, such as Ponder and viem, then retry instead of using a zero. A PR with integration tests will follow.

topPRs.title: feat(proxyd): serve local consensus state when shared HA state is stale
topPRs.author: zhwrd
topPRs.body:
Follows #782 (merged).

## Problem

With HA consensus, every node serves the shared state from Redis: the leader posts it, followers read it each heartbeat. A node that can't refresh it, typically because it can't reach Redis, keeps serving its last copy however old it gets. On 2026-10-22 (mn-uni-mainnet-0, 03:42–03:49 UTC) every pod on one node lost Redis. All three public pods were on that node, so the public endpoint served block 61891874 for ~8 min until the pods were rescheduled. The step-down fix in #782 doesn't help here, because a follower that can't reach Redis still has nothing newer to serve.

## Change

Off by default: nothing changes unless a backend group sets the new option.

- New backend group option **`consensus_ha_serve_local_when_stale`** (default `false`). When enabled, `GetState` and `GetCLSyncBody` serve the node's locally polled consensus state if its copy of the shared state is older than `lockPeriod` (default 30s) and the local state is valid. Once a refresh succeeds, the node serves the shared state again.
- New gauge **`proxyd_group_consensus_ha_serving_local{backend_group_name}`**: 1 while the node serves local state (always 0 with the option off). It's set every heartbeat, and the node logs when it switches either way (`shared consensus state is stale, serving local state` / `serving shared consensus state again`).

## Trade-off

This is why the option defaults to off. While a node serves local state, it can report a different head from its peers. That is the inconsistency HA consensus normally prevents, and clients spread across pods may see the head move backwards by a few blocks. We think that beats serving an arbitrarily stale head with HTTP 200. The new gauge makes this visible, and an alert can be added on it, e.g. `max_over_time(proxyd_group_consensus_ha_serving_local[5m]) == 1` for N minutes.

## Tests

`TestRedisConsensusTracker_ServesLocalWhenRemoteStale` covers:

- the shared state is served while fresh, even when the local state is ahead;
- the local state is served once the shared state is older than the lock period, and the gauge goes to 1;
- after Redis returns, the node serves the shared state again and the gauge goes back to 0;
- the stale shared state is still served when there is no valid local state.

`TestRedisConsensusTracker_ServesRemoteWhenStaleByDefault` checks that with the option off the stale shared state is still served and the gauge stays 0.

`go test -race ./...` passes in `proxyd`.

topPRs.title: fix(proxyd): step down as HA consensus leader when the lock cannot be confirmed
topPRs.author: zhwrd
topPRs.body:
## Bug

In `RedisConsensusTracker.stateHeartbeat`, when a leader failed to read the lock or to extend it, it tried to release the lock and **returned without clearing `ct.leader` if the release also failed**. Release fails in exactly the cases where leadership is lost:

- Redis is unreachable (`dial tcp ...: i/o timeout`), or
- another node has already taken the expired lock (`lock already taken, locked nodes: [0]`, redsync `ErrTaken`).

From then on every heartbeat repeats Extend fails → Unlock fails → return. The node never reaches the follower branch that reads the current leader's state, and `GetState()` keeps serving the last state it posted. Clients routed to that pod get a frozen `eth_blockNumber`, `null` for newer blocks, "beyond head" errors on `eth_getLogs`, and `latest` rewritten to the stale block, all with HTTP 200. The pod never recovers on its own.

## Incidents (2026-10-22)

- **tn-soneium-minato-0-proxyd-public**. At ~05:48 UTC a host network blip broke Redis for 2 of 3 pods. Leader g2blr lost the lock and npn47 took it at 05:49:10. After recovery g2blr logged `failed to extend lock` / `failed to release the lock after error: lock already taken, locked nodes: [0]` every ~500ms. Its `proxyd_group_consensus_ha_latest_block` stayed at 34726891 until the pod was deleted at ~06:12, ending ~678 blocks (~22 min) behind while serving ~1/3 of traffic.
- **tn-soneium-minato-0-proxyd-private**: pod nrhnb froze at the same block at the same time and was still stuck ~10.7h later.
- **mn-uni-mainnet-0-proxyd-public / -internal**, 03:42–03:49 UTC. Every pod on one node lost Redis, and two leaders hit the read-lock variant (`failed to release the lock after error: dial tcp ...:6379: i/o timeout`).

## Fix

Both failure paths now call `stepDown()`. It releases the lock on a best-effort basis and sets `leader = false` whether or not the release succeeds; a lock that can't be released expires after `lockPeriod`. On the next heartbeat the node follows the current leader.

This fixes the case where Redis comes back (Soneium). A node that still can't reach Redis keeps serving its last copy of the shared state; that is addressed in the follow-up PR #783.

## Tests

New `proxyd/consensus_tracker_redis_test.go` (miniredis):

- `StepsDownWhenLockTaken`: the lock expires and another node takes it, then extend and release both fail. Asserts the node steps down and serves the new leader's head.
- `RecoversFromRedisOutage`: the incident sequence (Redis drops, lock expires, another node takes over, Redis returns).

Both fail on the previous code (`node must step down ...`). `go test -race ./...` passes in `proxyd`.

topPRs.title: fix(proxyd): answer out-of-range state reads and log ranges with errors
topPRs.author: tremarkley
topPRs.body:
**Description**

In consensus mode, proxyd answers a request for a block above its consensus latest without forwarding it. Since #552 that answer has been a placeholder value for everything except block lookups:

- `"0x0"` for `eth_getBalance` and `eth_getTransactionCount`;
- `"0x"` code, zero storage, and `null` for `eth_call` and `eth_getProof`;
- `[]` for `eth_getLogs`, even when the range only partly crosses the head.

Clients can't tell those from real data. proxyd replicas each track their own consensus latest, so a client that reads at a head it just saw can hit this.

This change answers those requests with the error an execution client gives, keeping HTTP 200 as #552 intended:

- **State reads:** `-32001 block not found` (EIP-1898's "Resource not found", which op-reth returns).
- **`eth_getLogs` and `eth_newFilter`:** `-32602 block range extends beyond current head block`, which op-geth and op-reth both return for `eth_getLogs`.
- **Block lookups:** unchanged, still `null`.

These overridden responses now count in `proxyd_rpc_calls_total` under `status_code="400"`, following the existing convention for JSON-RPC errors sent with HTTP 200.

**Tests**

New `TestConsensus` cases cover every out-of-range state read, `eth_getLogs` ranges that are past or spanning the head, `eth_newFilter`, and a batch. Each case checks for the error code, no `result`, and no backend request. All of them fail on `main` with the placeholder values.

**Additional context**

This keeps #546's fix: future-block lookups still return `null` with HTTP 200, and no out-of-range answer is HTTP 400. Each error's own `HTTPErrorCode` sets the status (`writeRPCRes`). The removed `ErrBlockOutOfRange` set 400, and the new errors set none.

#546 also says `eth_getStorageAt` returns zeros for a future block. The clients don't do that. Each read below was sent past head to each client directly:

| Read past head | geth v1.17.8 | op-geth v1.101702.2 | op-reth v2.6 | proxyd with this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eth_getBlockByNumber` | `null` | `null` | `null` | `null` |
| `eth_getBalance`, `eth_getStorageAt`, `eth_getCode`, `eth_call` | `-32000 header not found` | `-32000 header not found` | `-32001 block not found` | `-32001 block not found` |
| `eth_getLogs` | `-32602 block range extends beyond current head block` | `-32602 block range extends beyond current head block` | `-32602 block range extends beyond current head block` | `-32602 block range extends beyond current head block` |

All of these answers are HTTP 200.

**Metadata**

- Fixes #768
- Keeps #546 fixed (block lookups return `null` with HTTP 200)

### Black: GitHub Action installs unvalidated required-version from pyproject.toml
[CVE-2026-114134](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-114134) / [GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

The GitHub Action bundled with Black can read the version from `tool.black.required-version` if `use_pyproject` is set to True. This version is not validated and therefore can be used to execute untrusted code in the context of a victim's repository.

##### Details

This is similar to the previous CVE-2026-31900. The value in `tool.black.required-version` is accepted as the version to be installed by the action without validation.

##### Proof of concept

Reproduction requires a victim to use Black's GitHub Action with `use_pyproject: true`. The attacker would then issue a PR to the victim's repository with `pyproject.toml` edited so that Black points to a malicious repository.

##### Impact

This is a remote code execution vulnerability impacting users using the GitHub Action bundled with psf/black and using the `use_pyproject: true` setting.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 8.7 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

#### References
- [https://github.com/psf/black/security/advisories/GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/security/advisories/GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2)
- [https://github.com/psf/black/pull/5510](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/pull/5510)
- [https://github.com/psf/black/commit/ac1f71563aeccf73cf13ece00f231d9d6c66a514](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/commit/ac1f71563aeccf73cf13ece00f231d9d6c66a514)
- [https://github.com/psf/black](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black)
- [https://github.com/psf/black/releases/tag/26.10.1](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/releases/tag/26.10.1)

This data is provided by [OSV](https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2) and the [GitHub Advisory Database](https://redirect.github.com/github/advisory-database) ([CC-BY 4.0](https://redirect.github.com/github/advisory-database/blob/main/LICENSE.md)).
</details>

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>psf/black (black)</summary>

### [`v26.10.1`](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/blob/HEAD/CHANGES.md#Version-26101)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/compare/26.10.0...26.10.1)

##### Highlights

This release fixes a security issue in Black's bundled GitHub Action. Repositories that
use the action are encouraged to update to the latest version of Black immediately. This
update is received automatically when using `psf/black@stable`, and is independent of
the version of Black installed by the action.

When the GitHub Action reads version specifiers from `tool.black.required-version`, it
now only accepts released versions of Black, as it already did for `black` requirements
in dependency lists. Other values, such as URL references, are now rejected. This issue
has been registered as `GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2`; a CVE identifier is pending.

##### Stable style

- Fix a long Jupyter notebook assignment magic (for example `x = !ls -la`) being wrapped
  in parentheses, which IPython can no longer run; such cells are now left unchanged
  ([#​5481](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5481))
- Keep repeated lines outside the selected `--line-ranges` unchanged ([#​5436](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5436))
- Fix `--line-ranges` formatting lines that follow a statement when formatting joins or
  re-indents that statement ([#​5484](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5484))
- Fix `--line-ranges` crashing with an internal error when an unselected statement has a
  `# fmt: skip` comment on the last line before a closing bracket ([#​5477](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5477))
- Prevent moving an encoding declaration (for example `# -*- coding: latin-1 -*-`) onto
  the first two lines of a file ([#​5487](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5487))
- Fix adding an extra trailing blank line inside a multi-line module docstring when its
  last line is near the line length limit ([#​5494](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5494))
- Keep the parentheses around a walrus that is the only item in a set (for example
  `{(x := f())}`) when targeting Python 3.9 or older, since Python 3.8 and 3.9.0 can't
  parse it without them ([#​5502](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5502))

##### Preview style

- Do not split short expressions on delimiters (such as binary operators, comparisons,
  or comprehensions) inside brackets when preceded by a standalone comment ([#​5455](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5455))
- Fix the unstable `string_processing` feature removing backslash-newline sequences from
  raw strings, which changed their value ([#​5482](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5482))
- Avoid adding unnecessary parentheses around unbreakable right-hand side expressions in
  assignments (such as annotated assignments or subscript targets) ([#​5473](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5473))
- Parenthesize expressions with parameter comments when they exceed the line length
  under `--preview` ([#​5442](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5442))
- Fix `wrap_long_dict_values_in_parens` dropping the parentheses around a right-hand
  side that contains a dictionary, leaving a line over the length limit ([#​5492](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5492))
- Fix the unstable `string_processing` feature adding a space after `*` or `**` in a PEP
  695 type parameter (`* Ts = ...`) when it splits a string in the parameter's default
  ([#​5504](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5504))
- Avoid unnecessary line splits of trailers (such as indexing/subscripts) when an
  earlier bracket split exceeds the line length only due to a trailing comment ([#​5498](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5498))

##### Configuration

- Add `--cache-dir` to configure the cache directory from the command line ([#​5433](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5433))
- Don't cache a file as formatted after formatting or checking it with `--line-ranges`,
  which made a later full `black --check` pass and `black` skip the unformatted lines
  ([#​5476](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5476))
- Respect a `.gitignore` that starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark. The mark became part
  of the first pattern, so that pattern never matched and Black formatted files that git
  ignores ([#​5497](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5497))

##### Performance

- Avoid quadratic runtime when splitting very long lines with many trailing bracket
  pairs (such as consecutive subscripts) ([#​5475](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5475))

##### Integrations

- Fix the GitHub Action crashing on dependency-group includes when `use_pyproject` is
  enabled ([#​5479](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5479))
- When the GitHub Action reads version specifiers from `tool.black.required-version`, it
  now only accepts released versions of Black, as it already did for `black`
  requirements in dependency lists. Other values, such as URL references, are now
  rejected. ([#​5510](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5510))

### [`v26.10.0`](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/blob/HEAD/CHANGES.md#Version-26100)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/compare/26.5.1...26.10.0)

##### Preview style

##### New preview features

- Add missing blank lines after classes whose last method has an ellipsis body ([#​5439](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5439))

  (e.g. `x[key] = expr`) ([#​5095](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5095))
- Parenthesize tuple expressions in `yield` statements for consistency with function
  calls and returns ([#​5170](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5170))
- Stop splitting between a variable and its operator (`not in`, `==`, `is`, ...) when
  the right-hand side is a bracketed expression, and instead split inside the brackets
  ([#​5135](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5135))
- In `.pyi` stub files, enforce a blank line after a function or method that has a
  docstring-only body when another comment or statement follows it ([#​5158](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5158))

##### Updates to existing preview features

- Fix crash in stub files when `# fmt: skip` is placed on a function in a group of
  same-name decorated functions (e.g. `@overload`s or a property setter) ([#​5430](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5430))
- Keep the parentheses around a lambda used as the iterable of a comprehension (e.g.
  `[x for x in (lambda: 0) if x]`) ([#​5176](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5176), [#​5200](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5200))

##### Updates to existing unstable features

- Do not treat multi-line expressions with merged strings and trailing `# type: ignore`
  comments as single-line unsplittable expressions ([#​5466](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5466))
- Fix duplicated inline comment when stripping the parentheses around a string or
  merging a backslash-continued string on the same line ([#​5449](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5449))
- Split long stringified return annotations even when the function has parameters
  ([#​5427](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5427))
- Don't hug brackets when doing so would join two `# type: ignore` comments onto one
  line ([#​5271](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5271))
- Fix a crash when `# type: ignore` is lost during formatting of a long parenthesized
  string ([#​5329](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5329))
- Fix only the first part of an implicitly concatenated unmergeable string (e.g.
  `r"..." r"..."`) being wrapped in parentheses ([#​5434](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5434))

##### Configuration

- Add support for `NO_COLOR` environment variable to disable ANSI output ([#​5129](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5129))
- Remove spurious target version warning when runtime version is included in a
  `--target-version` flag ([#​5167](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5167))
- Fix `--force-exclude` not excluding files whose path contains `..` (e.g.
  `black ../generated/file.py` run from a subdirectory) ([#​5471](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5471))
- Fall back to the default configuration, with a warning, when the given sources share
  no common project root (e.g. they are on different drives on Windows) instead of
  crashing ([#​5386](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5386))
- Fix loading a stale cached `pyproject.toml` path when `--code` is used from different
  working directories in the same process ([#​5152](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5152))
- Add validation for `--line-ranges` values ([#​5107](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5107))
- Ignore empty cache files instead of raising an `EOFError` ([#​5192](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5192))
- Reject non-string `include` and `force-exclude` values in `pyproject.toml` ([#​5193](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5193))
- Validate `BLACK_NUM_WORKERS` values and report invalid values as usage errors instead
  of crashing ([#​5211](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5211))
- Ignore permission errors when reading cache ([#​5258](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5258))

##### Packaging

- Reduce the size of Linux standalone binaries by stripping debug symbols during the
  PyInstaller release build ([#​5223](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5223))
- Black is now released using GitHub
  [Immutable Releases](https://docs.github.com/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/immutable-releases)
  ([#​5296](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5296))

##### Performance

- Fix superlinear runtime growth with the number of input files ([#​5450](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5450))
- Improve performance on strings containing many consecutive backslashes ([#​5163](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5163))
- Improve performance on files with many `# fmt: skip`/`# fmt: off`/`# fmt: on` comments
  ([#​5169](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5169), [#​5190](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5190), [#​5232](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5232))
- Improve performance on long calls and collections ([#​5177](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5177))
- Improve performance on multiline strings inside large collections (e.g. a dict literal
  with triple-quoted strings as values) ([#​5188](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5188))
- Improve performance on files with many soft keywords (e.g. `match`/`case` blocks)
  ([#​5186](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5186))
- Improve performance on long semicolon-separated statements (in the stable style) and
  large dict literals (in `--preview`) ([#​5184](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5184))
- Improve performance of `--line-ranges` on files with many sibling blocks (a long
  `if`/`elif` chain, a `match` with many cases, or many top-level definitions) ([#​5213](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5213))
- Improve performance on deeply nested bracketed expressions ([#​5171](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5171), [#​5242](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5242))
- Improve performance on lists and subscripts holding one long expression without
  operators (e.g. a long run of implicitly concatenated strings inside `[]`) ([#​5239](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5239))
- Improve performance on deeply chained operations (e.g. a long `a ** b ** c ** ...`
  chain) ([#​5235](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5235))
- Improve performance on long `if`/`elif` chains and other compound statements with many
  clauses ([#​5322](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5322))
- Improve performance of `string_processing`:
  - when merging implicitly concatenated f-strings containing long string literals
    ([#​5165](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5165))
  - when merging long implicitly concatenated strings ([#​5173](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5173), [#​5194](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5194))
  - when rewriting large nodes (e.g. `"%s ..." % (a, b, c, ...)`) ([#​5178](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5178), [#​5199](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5199), [#​5220](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5220))
  - when splitting long string literals ([#​5183](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5183))

##### Output

- Report parser failures using editor-friendly `path:line:column` locations ([#​5237](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5237))
- Fix crash when writing formatted code or diffs to a `sys.stdout` that has no `buffer`
  attribute (e.g. in Jupyter notebooks) ([#​5411](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5411))
- Report parse failures on Black's own output as internal errors ([#​5383](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5383))

## Summary

Reverts the glibc 2.43 constraint from #780. Other Wolfi packages, such as perl, are built against glibc 2.44, so pinning glibc 2.43 leaves the image with an inconsistent libc and breaks them.

## Summary

Pins glibc in `circleci-runner-wolfi` to the 2.43-r13 family so the image no longer resolves to glibc 2.44. Binaries built in the runner stay compatible with Ubuntu 24.04 based CircleCI executors (glibc 2.39).
